results.name: Agility Ladder in in Out Out
instructions: Stand facing the agility ladder.
Step into the first square with one foot, then the other.
Step out to the sides of the next square with one foot, then the other.
Keep repeating in, in, out, out quickly along the ladder.
tips: Stay on the balls of your feet.
Pump your arms to keep the rhythm.
results.description: Agility Ladder in in Out Out is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Adductors, Abductors.

results.name: Air Punches March
instructions: Stand tall with your back straight and feet shoulder-width apart.
Make fists of your hands, fold one arm at your side and extend the other arm overhead.
Raise one of your thighs while bending your knee, and lower your arm while extending the other arm overhead.
Return to the initial position and repeat by raising your other thigh.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and stability throughout the exercise.
Perform the movements with controlled, deliberate motions to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you punch upwards and inhaling as you bring your arm back.
results.description: Air Punches March is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Glutes, Chest.

results.name: Air Swing Running
instructions: Place your feet on the footplates of the suspended legs.
Hold onto the handle bars for stability.
Glide your left leg forward in a swift motion, while extending your right leg backward swiftly.
Alternate your legs, maintaining a smooth and controlled running motion.
tips: Bend your elbows slightly and support your body with your shoulders depressed.
Maintain an upright posture without leaning excessively forward or backward.
Perform the movement at a pace that allows you to maintain proper technique.
results.description: Air Swing Running is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Biceps, Triceps.

results.name: Air Swing Side to Side Swing
instructions: Place your feet on the footplates.
Grip the parallel bars with your hands for stability.
Keeping your legs together swing them from one side to the other.
Continue alternating from side to side in a smooth manner.
tips: Keep your shoulders depressed and elbows slightly bended when gripping the side bars.
Move your legs swiftly but smoothly to the side, pivoting at the hips.
Keep your torso straight, avoid rotating your spine.
Perform the movement in a controlled manner, without using excessive momentum.
results.description: Air Swing Side to Side Swing is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Biceps, Triceps.

results.name: Air Swing Walking
instructions: Place your feet on the footplates of the suspended legs.
Hold onto the handle bars for stability.
Glide your left leg forward, while extending your right leg backward.
Alternate your legs, maintaining a smooth and steady walking pace.
tips: Bend your elbows slightly and support your body with your shoulders depressed.
Maintain an upright posture without leaning excessively forward or backward.
Perform the movement at a pace that allows you to maintain proper technique.
results.description: Air Swing Walking is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Biceps, Triceps.

results.name: Alternate Punching
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your hands held up in a guard position near your chest.
Punch forward with your right arm, rotating your upper torso slightly.
Return your right hand to the guard position and punch forward with your left arm, again rotating your upper torso slightly.
Continue alternating punches in a rhythmic manner.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and stability throughout the exercise.
Focus on snapping your punches out quickly and returning your hands to the guard position to maintain proper form.
Maintain a slight bend in your knees to absorb the impact and enhance stability.
results.description: Alternate Punching is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Core, Upper Back.

results.name: Alternating Hamstring Curl With Punch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms bent at a 90-degree angle with fists close to your chest.
Curl your right leg back, bringing your heel towards your glutes while simultaneously punching forward with your left arm.
Lower your right leg and return your left arm to the starting position.
Curl your left leg back, bringing your heel towards your glutes while punching forward with your right arm. Continue alternating sides.
tips: Focus on squeezing your hamstrings and glutes as you curl your leg to enhance muscle activation.
Keep a steady rhythm to ensure both sides of your body are working evenly.
Maintain a strong and upright posture to avoid unnecessary strain on your back.
results.description: Alternating Hamstring Curl With Punch is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Hip Flexors, Chest.

results.name: Alternating Hamstring Curl
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, keeping both arms bent by your sides.
Shift your weight onto your left leg and bend your right knee, bringing your heel towards your glutes, squeezing your hamstring at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower your right leg back to the starting position with control.
Repeat the movement with your left leg. Alternate between right and left legs for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce injury risk.
Ensure your knees stay aligned and avoid twisting your hips.
Use a full range of motion, bringing your heel as close to your glutes as possible.
results.description: Alternating Hamstring Curl is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Calves.

results.name: Ankle Circles
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, hands at your hips.
Lift your right foot off the floor slightly and rotate your ankle in a circular motion, making small controlled circles.
After a set number of rotations, switch direction and rotate your ankle in the opposite direction.
Repeat the movement with your left ankle, rotating in both directions.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and stability throughout the exercise.
Ensure your leg remains still and only your ankle is moving to focus on the targeted muscles.
Perform the exercise for an equal amount of time or repetitions in both directions to ensure balanced muscle development.
results.description: Ankle Circles is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shins.

results.name: Ankle Dorsal Flexion
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your hands resting on your hips or at your sides for balance.
Flex both feet simultaneously, bringing your toes towards your shins, and then return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement, flexing and relaxing both feet simultaneously.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and stability throughout the exercise.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Focus on the movement of your ankles and avoid using your leg muscles to assist.
results.description: Ankle Dorsal Flexion is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Calves.
